annotation.kind: static reconstruction of Theorem 3.1 with derived MGS dimension selection, source-level Algorithm 2 modules, raw Appendix-A sensitivity gains, explicit Frobenius-condition-number interpretation, and qualitative first-order semantics

assumptions: The dimension n is positive, A and the left preconditioner ML have certified inverses, b is nonzero, and xExact solves A*xExact=b.
The search spaces form an increasing full-column-rank basis family, and the raw equations and data for Algorithm 2's four modules are supplied at every positive dimension k<=n.

At the dimension selected by the MGS argument, the forward bound is conditional on equations (3.2)-(3.4), the MGS/Givens least-squares perturbation model, numerical nonsingularity, and the qualitative conditions (3.5)-(3.6).
The cited MGS law states only that dimension one is well conditioned and loss at k+1 forces the input-near-dependence condition (A.1) at k; it supplies no selected dimension.
The reusable Appendix-A interface is uniform in k and MR and supplies a contribution expansion with raw gains in the actual module-relative errors, not the collected bound (3.8).
The unspecified c(n,k) is represented at each fixed dimension by a nonnegative scalar at least one; no coefficients or polynomial degree are invented.
The qualitative meanings of much-less-than-one and omitted second-order terms are parameterized because the paper gives no threshold or asymptotic variable.
All matrix and vector quantities are real, so exceptional floating-point values and range failures are outside the model.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P19 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p19_t2_modular_gmres_forward_error {n : Nat} (semantics : P19FirstOrderSemantics) (family : P19Theorem31Family n semantics) (mgs : P19MGSSelectionLaw family) (appendix : P19StaticAppendixATheory family) : exists k : P19Theorem31Dimension n, p19IterationWellConditioned (family.iteration k) and (P19Algorithm2Conditions (family.iteration k) -> forall MR MRinv (hMR : p19InversePair MR MRinv), let q := appendix.rightQuantities k MR MRinv hMR; p19FirstOrderLe semantics (p19ForwardError family.system.xExact (family.iteration k).xHat) ((family.iteration k).dimensionFactor * p19StaticXi MR MRinv q * p19ConditionNumberF (p19StaticSplitOperator family.system MRinv) (p19StaticSplitInverse family.system MR)))
formal_statement.plain_language: There exists a dimension k no larger than n at which the computed MGS basis satisfies both 4/3 conditioning bounds; when Algorithm 2's stated error and smallness conditions hold at that dimension, every nonsingular analytical right preconditioner gives the normalized first-order forward-error bound with the exact alpha, beta, lambda, and xi formulas.

informal_proof: If dimension n is well conditioned, select it. Otherwise choose the first dimension whose computed MGS basis is not well conditioned; dimension one is good, so its predecessor is positive, remains good by minimality, and satisfies (A.1) by the cited loss-of-orthogonality law. Assuming Algorithm 2's stated conditions at that selected dimension, for arbitrary MR obtain the uniform Appendix-A raw expansion, derive each safe relative module error from (3.2)-(3.4), apply the four raw sensitivity gains and the Euclidean triangle inequality, collect exactly alpha*epsilonC + beta*epsilonB + beta*ug + lambda*epsilonX, and retain the source-classified second-order remainder.
informal_statement: The complete static modular attainable-forward-error result of Theorem 3.1, including a derived existential MGS dimension and explicit qualitative first-order semantics.

tier_rationale: The target combines a paper-scoped finite first-loss search, the cited MGS loss law, Algorithm 2's four modular bounds, safe relative-error normalization, the raw Appendix-A sensitivity expansion, coefficient algebra, and several Euclidean norm steps. The L construction materially uses NumStability.vecNorm2_add_le and NumStability.vecNorm2_nonneg, while the frozen library provides none of the P19-specific selection or propagation framework.
